  "title": "Auctioned Time",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #22 Auctioned Time: reusable adult idea-source engine that generates charity-auction premises where {{char}} volunteers a clearly defined block of time, skill or service and {{user}} wins the slot for the fundraiser's benefit. Varies the service, cause, acquisition format, prior acquaintance, boundary style and what the win does and does not entitle.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",
    "version": "0.4",
    "entry": "22",
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "At a fundraiser, charity auction or similar event, adult {{char}} volunteers a clearly defined block of her time, skill or service — a dinner, a lesson, a guided day, a practical job — and {{user}} wins or otherwise receives the slot, with the payment going to the fundraiser rather than to {{char}}. The engine is the collision between a bounded charitable arrangement and whatever the two adults actually are to each other: strangers, coworkers, rivals, acquaintances or near-friends. The bid buys the service and nothing else; where it leads is open. Mirrored versions can reverse who volunteered the service.",
  "core_premise": "At a fundraiser, charity auction or similar event, {{char}} volunteers a clearly defined block of her time, skill or service. {{user}} wins or otherwise receives the slot, with the payment going to the fundraiser rather than directly purchasing {{char}}. The win conveys only the service actually volunteered; anything beyond it is a separate decision both adults would have to make freely. Mirrored versions can reverse who volunteered the service, and the same boundary rules apply in either direction.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening around the auctioned lot. Specify the fundraiser and its cause, the exact service {{char}} volunteered and its terms — duration, location, limits — how the lot was sold, and what {{char}} and {{user}} are to each other beforehand, if anything. Establish why she volunteered and whether either expected a different winner. Begin near the moment the engine activates — the hammer falling, the ticket drawn, the handover, the first scheduled slot — and leave {{user}}'s reaction, the delivery of the service and every eventual outcome open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Fundraiser purpose and beneficiary: hospital, shelter, brigade, club, library, clinic or disaster relief",
    "The service actually volunteered: dinner, lesson, guided trip, repair day, sitting, workshop or other defined skill",
    "Duration and shape of the time sold: one hour, one evening, sessions, a day, open-dated within a year",
    "Acquisition format: public auction, silent auction, raffle, sealed bids, online listing, fixed-price draw or committee matching",
    "Whether {{user}} and {{char}} already know each other, and as what: strangers, coworkers, neighbours, classmates, rivals, family friends",
    "Whether the service is practical, social, creative or recreational in character",
    "How formal the arrangement is: written terms, printed conditions card, handshake, committee mediation, voucher",
    "Whether either party expected the winning bidder or donor to be someone else",
    "Why {{char}} volunteered: devotion to the cause, guilt, showcase, dare, PR, tradition, grief, repayment",
    "Whether {{char}} delivers the service professionally or personally, and how that line is drawn",
    "Whether the slot happens once or repeats, and who controls scheduling and rescheduling",
    "Whether the payment was large, token, contested or anonymous, and what that means to each of them",
    "Who else is watching: rival bidders, friends, partners, committee, local press",
    "Whether the mirrored version applies with {{user}} as the donor of the service",
    "What happens after the slot: friendship, follow-up offers, professional relationship, quiet ending or nothing",
    "Whether anyone tries to expand the scope, and how the agreed boundary holds or is renegotiated"
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "The winner receives only the service actually volunteered. Payment to a fundraiser does not create sexual access, romance, ownership or permission to expand the scope. If both adults later choose something beyond the auctioned service, treat it as a separate decision.",
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions or future behaviour unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; a buyer who assumes the win entitles him to more is wrong, and {{char}}'s guesses about {{user}} are only guesses.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, rescheduling, friendship, romance, complaint and every other player choice open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "The auction result is a commercial and charitable fact, not a romantic or sexual one; it creates an appointment, not a relationship.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "Roles do not remove autonomy: donor, winner, volunteer, teacher, guide and client are roles within the event, not ownership.",
    "{{char}}'s future is not predetermined; she may enjoy the slot, endure it, renegotiate it, or treat it as pure obligation.",
    "Wealth, generosity of the bid and status in the room do not make {{user}} or any bidder morally, romantically or sexually superior.",
    "Volunteering the service is {{char}}'s free and bounded decision; she sets duration, location and limits, and may withdraw or renegotiate under the lot's own terms.",
    "If {{char}} offers anything beyond the auctioned service — a second block, a coffee, her number — it is a new, separate, revocable choice, not a consequence of the bid.",
    "If the lot is professional in character, keep professional standards and professional boundaries; a client relationship creates no personal access.",
    "If a version includes an existing partner for {{char}} or a rival bidder, their knowledge, feelings and consent are separate facts to establish, not defaults.",
    "Distinguish the public spectacle of the auction from the private reality of the service; teasing from the room does not redefine what was sold.",
    "Do not force romance, attraction or resentment into every instance; a pleasant transaction, a dull afternoon or an ordinary professional exchange are all valid outcomes.",
    "The service should be concrete and skilful rather than a vague 'date'; specify the craft, lesson, trip or task and let competence or the lack of it show.",
    "Mirrored versions reverse who donated and who won without changing the boundary rules in either direction.",
    "The beneficiary of the money is the fundraiser, not {{char}}; keep the charitable frame visible and meaningful rather than a thin excuse.",
    "{{char}} should remain a person beyond the lot: occupation, friends, humour, worries and a life the auction does not touch.",
    "Do not treat the bid size as a measure of {{user}}'s worth or of {{char}}'s gratitude; small bids, raffle luck and anonymous wins are equally valid.",
    "Keep ground truth about intent separate from the room's gossip and each character's interpretation of it.",
    "Open at a playable moment — bidding, the hammer, the handover, the first scheduled slot — without scripting {{user}}'s reaction or the eventual outcome."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "Preserve the user-agency rules from Series Bibles I and II. Do not define {{user}}'s personality, attraction, feelings, dialogue, consent, decisions, or future behaviour unless the supplied concept explicitly establishes a fact. A character may make assumptions about {{user}}, but those assumptions are not objective truth.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Characters may want, invite, tempt, pressure, negotiate, confess, lie, tease, manipulate, hope, or plan, but whether {{user}} cooperates, rejects them, exposes them, forgives them, leaves, joins them, or changes course remains roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults. Sexual openness, nudity, promiscuity, virginity, flirtatiousness, clothing style, exhibitionism, confidence, loyalty, and romantic attachment are independent traits. Do not infer one automatically from another.",
    "Consent is activity-specific. Agreement to look does not imply permission to touch, photograph, record, or have sex. Housing, money, cohabitation, one bed, professional services, adult-industry work, prior sex, or an existing affair do not create blanket consent.",
    "Keep ground truth separate from character rationalisation. A buyer may believe a winning bid bought him influence, and a donor may believe her generosity obliges gratitude. Those are beliefs, not narrator-endorsed facts.",
    "Do not force romance into friendship, workplace, shared-hobby, historical, or chance-encounter series. Friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual sex, unresolved tension, or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Characters should remain people outside their hook. A kink, occupation, reputation, relationship status, or unusual setup can be important without becoming the only thing they talk about.",
    "A winning bid buys exactly the volunteered service and nothing else; any extension of scope requires {{char}}'s separate, unpressured, revocable agreement.",
    "{{char}} sets the boundaries of her own donated lot — duration, location, conduct, company — and may end or renegotise within its stated terms at any time.",
    "An outbid rival, jealous partner or teasing crowd has no authority over {{char}}'s personal life regardless of what the auction looked like.",
    "If the service is professional, professional boundaries apply; the charitable discount does not downgrade or upgrade the client relationship into anything personal by default.",
    "No humiliation, debt, servitude or ownership follows from the auction; keep the charitable, bounded, adult character of the arrangement intact."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Fundraiser cause: hospital, animal shelter, fire brigade, university club, community centre, disaster relief, school, sports club, library, arts scholarship, lifeboat, rural clinic",
    "Service offered: home cooking, dance, language, photography, personal training, gardening, pottery, board games, fishing, guitar, DIY, wine tasting, coding, portraiture, car detailing, hiking",
    "Acquisition format: live auction, silent auction, raffle, sealed bids, online auction, gala paddle, experience draw, fixed-price drive, promises night, workplace auction, tombola, committee matching",
    "Prior acquaintance: strangers, coworkers, classmates, neighbours, rivals, friend's sister, local celebrity, former tutor, boss, shop regular, mutual friends, wedding acquaintance",
    "Volunteer motive: devotion, guilt, showcase, dare, PR, secret hope, tradition, grief, rivalry, substitution, curiosity, courage, committee debt, belief, reciprocity, protest",
    "Formality: written contract, conditions card, handshake, committee mediation, voucher, refund clause, no-extension rule, professional standard, casual terms, chaperone, public-only, venue rules, single meeting, reschedules, plus-one clause, dry-house terms",
    "Duration: one hour, one evening, three sessions, weekly month, weekend day, dawn trip, at-her-pace, open-dated year, ninety minutes, half day, split hours, single dinner, month of lessons, event pairing, timeboxed, travel day",
    "Formal gala versus pub raffle versus online listing versus workplace event",
    "Practical versus social versus creative versus recreational service character",
    "Professional delivery versus personal gift of time",
    "Whether {{user}} expected to win, bid impulsively, was sponsored, or won by luck",
    "Whether {{char}} expected a different winner and how she handles the surprise",
    "Onlookers: rival bidders, friends, existing partners, committee, local press, nobody at all",

    "Aftermath: friendship, professional relationship, follow-up offer, refund, quiet ending, slow burn — all open, none required"
